mutations.label: S1 the `continue` that ends the expected branch is removed, so a group of screens that legitimately SHARE one route also gets #713's defect warning and is recorded in `identical_captures_713`. That is #718's entire subject -- the corpus's commonest sharing called a routing failure. The block still contains the word `continue` (the `len(_names713) < 2` guard above uses one), so the text assertion holds
S3 the detector stops looking at PAIRS (`< 2` becomes `< 3`), so two screens with a byte-identical capture are neither reported nor recorded. No string any test asserts on changes

S2 EXPECTED-MISSED (dead default, not a gap): the `.get(n, "")` fallback is unreachable. `_routes713` is built from the same `results` that populate `_by713`, and `_by713` only holds names that were truthy in that same loop, so every name looked up here is already a key. Both the real default and the mutated one are therefore never used; the mutation changes nothing a test could observe.
